# MarkAlign

> A grading-alignment demo and evaluation harness. It learns one teacher's marking
> standard from 25 essays they scored on one assignment, grades new essays the same
> way with every score pinned to verbatim quotes from the student's text, and — the
> actual point — measures whether the AI agrees with the teacher for the right
> reasons. Made by Moinuddin Shaik.

Key facts (measured, not claimed; all reproducible from the repo):

- Score agreement on ASAP set 7: QWK 0.664 on 120 held-out essays vs one human
  rater — 92% of the 0.72 ceiling at which two trained human raters agree with
  each other. Learned from 25 calibration essays, no fine-tuning.
- Method: per-trait yes/no "checklist ladders" learned from the teacher's own
  examples (score = count of passed bars, each pinned to a verbatim quote), plus
  a computed score-distribution floor so the ladder matches how the teacher
  actually uses the scale.
- Generalization (ASAP set 1, different genre/scale/raters): raw QWK 0.369; the
  eval diagnosed a systematic generous offset and prescribed linear calibration
  in advance, recovering 0.576 (80% of that set's 0.721 ceiling). The
  calibrate/don't-calibrate rule is 3-for-3 across model/dataset cases.
- Current scope: the learned profile entangles teacher and task (all calibration
  essays answer one assignment). Cross-task teacher transfer is deliberately not
  claimed; it requires the same identified grader on two assignments, which
  public data lacks.
- Honest limits are documented in the README: confidence is anti-calibrated (the
  abstention gate's signal doesn't work yet), reasoning-agreement is a method
  without ground truth, results are one held-out split.

## Links

- [Live demo](https://markalign.up.railway.app): four real ASAP essays pre-graded
  against the learned standard (instant, cached); paste any essay to grade it
  live (rate-limited).
- [Source & eval](https://github.com/CodeWithMoin/markalign): full pipeline,
  frozen result snapshots in results/, reproducible via Makefile targets.
- [Author](https://moinuddin.app): Moinuddin Shaik.
